# Rosa Delgado — 58F | T2DM + HTN | 3-month follow-up (prep)

**One-liner:** A1c rising on MAXIMAL metformin (7.1% → 7.9% → 8.4% over ~11 mo); home BP averaging 148/92 on two agents; NEW microalbuminuria (UACR 62). This is a 'second-agent + intensify BP' visit, not a metformin-dose tweak.

## Trends that matter (not just the latest value)
| Date | A1c | BP |
|---|---|---|
| Jul 2025 | 7.1% | 146/90 (office) |
| Jan 2026 | 7.9% | 148/92 (office) |
| Jun 2026 | **8.4%** | **148/92 (home avg)** |

- A1c up **+1.3 points** on metformin 1000 mg BID — already max → **monotherapy failure**.
- BP above the **<130/80** diabetes target at *every* check, already on 2 agents → uncontrolled.

## Why this is more than 'rising sugar'
- **UACR 62 mg/g (Apr 2026) + eGFR 68** = early diabetic kidney disease (A2). This makes an **SGLT2 inhibitor the guideline-preferred second agent** (cardio-renal protection), independent of glucose. **GLP-1 RA** is the alternative and would also help weight (BMI 31.2).
- **LDL 118 on atorvastatin 40** — above the <70 diabetes goal; statin not yet optimized.

## Guideline-aligned next steps to tee up
1. **Add a second glucose-lowering agent — SGLT2 inhibitor preferred** given albuminuria (GLP-1 RA if weight/cost favor it). Metformin stays.
2. **Intensify antihypertensives** — add a CCB (e.g., amlodipine) or revisit regimen toward <130/80.
3. **Optimize lipids** — consider higher-intensity statin ± ezetimibe for LDL <70.

## Confirm BEFORE escalating
- Adherence + pharmacy refill history (true failure vs missed doses)
- Home BP technique/cuff; SGLT2 cautions (genital/UTI infections, volume, DKA history)
- Eye exam and foot exam up to date?

## Quick flags
- ⚠️ Sulfa allergy on chart, but **tolerates HCTZ (a sulfonamide)** — reconcile.
- ⚠️ K 4.2, eGFR 68 — safe ranges for adding SGLT2i and adjusting BP meds.

# Walter Okonkwo — 76M | Chronic-care follow-up + post-urgent-care recheck

**One-liner:** 76M on **11 chronic meds**. An urgent care started **clarithromycin 500 mg BID (06/19/2026)** for a sinus infection while he stays on **simvastatin 40 mg nightly** — a *contraindicated* CYP3A4 combination that sharply raises his risk of muscle injury/rhabdomyolysis.

## TOP ACTION — drug interaction (do this visit)
- **Why it matters (plain language):** Clarithromycin blocks the liver enzyme (CYP3A4) that clears simvastatin, so the statin can build up to several times its normal level. That can cause painful muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) that can injure the kidneys — **higher risk here because he's 76 with stage-3 CKD.**
- **Fix — pick ONE:**
  1. **Hold simvastatin** for the remaining days of the antibiotic (simplest; a short statin pause is safe), **or**
  2. **Switch the antibiotic** to azithromycin or doxycycline (don't inhibit CYP3A4, and both are penicillin-safe), **or**
  3. Temporarily switch to **pravastatin/rosuvastatin** (not cleared by CYP3A4).
- **Ask:** new muscle aches, weakness, or dark/cola urine? Check **CK** if any symptoms (baseline CK 132, Feb 2026 — none since).

## Watch — second interaction in the same list
- Clarithromycin also raises **apixaban** levels (CYP3A4 + P-gp) -> **bleeding risk**; and can raise **amlodipine** -> low BP/edema. Screen for bruising/bleeding and dizziness until the antibiotic is finished.

## Active problems
HTN | T2DM (A1c **7.8 ↑**) | CAD s/p RCA stent 2019 | paroxysmal AF (apixaban, CHA2DS2-VASc 4) | **CKD3a (eGFR 52)** | hypothyroid | BPH | GERD | gout

## Allergy
**Penicillin** (childhood hives) — this drove the urgent care's macrolide choice. Doxycycline is a penicillin-safe AND non-interacting alternative if the sinusitis still needs treatment. Worth characterizing the reaction.

## Process note
Urgent care did **not** reconcile the full med list (patient couldn't name his meds). Reinforce: carry the current med list — especially the blood thinner and statin — to every ER/urgent-care visit.
